the development of an in-vivo model for the study of cerebral oedemata in relation to intracerebral hemorrhage.

immunosuppression by radiation therapy does not protect against cerebral oedema after intracerebral hemorrhage.

immunosuppression by whole body irradiation protects against cerebral ischaemic damage and oedema in an animal model of intracranial haemorrhage, and that this protection is not mediated through a reduction of circulating white cell count or thrombocyte count.

the immunosuppression of the host by whole body irradiation is associated with a significant reduction in the development of cerebral ischaemia, cerebral oedema and brain tissue necrosis.
the development of cerebral ischaemia, oedema and haemorrhage is a complex process involving the interaction of many factors, including the immune system.
the development of cerebral ischaemia in the rat model of intracellular haemorrhage is associated with the development of oedema, and that this can be prevented by immunosuppression.

the use of radiation as an immunomodulatory agent to reduce cerebral oedema and improve outcome in ICH is not likely to be beneficial.
